newsitem.title: USA: U.S. prosecutors end probe of Rep. Enid Greene.
newsitem.headline: U.S. prosecutors end probe of Rep. Enid Greene.

text.p: Federal prosecutors Thursday formally cleared Utah Republican Representative Enid Greene, whose ex-husband has pleaded guilty to election fraud in her 1994 campaign and other criminal charges.

"The investigation into alleged criminal conduct by Representative Enid Greene was closed today and no criminal charges are being filed against the congresswoman," U.S. Attorney Eric Holder said in a brief statement.
He said the investigation had focused on allegations relating to her congressional campaigns in 1992 and 1994 and to her personal and family finances, including her federal tax returns.

Greene was a rising Republican star in Congress until late last year when her then-husband, Joseph Waldholtz, briefly disappeared after questions were raised about the couple's tangled finances. She decided not to seek re-election.
Greene maintained that Waldholtz, a former Republican political operative from Pennsylvania, had duped her and that she did nothing wrong.
Greene, who won office as a champion of family values, got a divorce on June 5, the day that Waldholtz pleaded guilty.
As treasurer for Greene's 1994 campaign for Congress Waldholtz admitted he filed false federal reports about contributions received.
He also pleaded guilty to making false statements to the federal election agency, causing his then-wife to file a false tax return in 1993 and bank fraud for a check-kiting scheme.

A federal judge last month ordered Waldholtz to jail after prosecutors said he had used herion, bounced checks and stole money from family and friends since June. The judge revoked his bond ahead of sentencing, set for November 7.
Prosecutors previously admitted the new allegations had severely damaged Waldholtz's credibility and that he no longer was of any use in the probe of Greene's campaign finances.
Although the prosecutors ended their investigation, Holder said the decision does not affect a continuing probe by the Federal Election Commission into Greene's 1992 and 1994 campaigns.
